findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No immutable audit logging is configured for write operations. The SAM template does not define CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs retention policies, or S3 bucket with object lock. The Lambda function does not log write operations with principal attribution. The schema documents this gap for deleteProduct.
findings.gap: Write operations (upsertProduct, deleteProduct) are not logged with authenticated principal attribution in an immutable, tamper-evident store.
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit logging in resolvers capturing principal, operation, target SKU, and timestamp. Configure immutable log storage (CloudWatch Logs with retention + S3 Object Lock, or CloudTrail data events).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging for write operations.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 is a conditional BLOCKER under write-enabled scope. This system exposes mutations (upsertProduct, deleteProduct) but has no immutable audit trail capturing which agent/user performed each mutation.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add structured audit logging in resolvers capturing JWT claims (principal), operation type, target SKU, and ISO timestamp.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every mutation logs {principal, action, resource, timestamp} to an immutable store with defined retention.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: The system extracts JWT claims from API Gateway authorizer context and uses scopes for authorization. However, there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own service identity vs. acting on behalf of a specific human user. No token exchange or on-behalf-of flow is implemented.
findings.gap: Cannot differentiate agent-as-self calls from agent-on-behalf-of-user calls. All authenticated callers are treated identically based on scopes alone.
findings.recommendation: Implement distinct authentication flows for agent-as-self (client_credentials) and agent-on-behalf-of-user (authorization_code with token exchange), and enforce different permission boundaries for each mode.

compensating_controls: Use distinct Cognito app clients for agent vs user identities, differentiating by client_id claim
Add a custom claim or header (X-On-Behalf-Of) to propagate user context

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: Both mutations use unconditional DynamoDB writes. upsertProduct uses PutItem without a condition expression (last-writer-wins). deleteProduct uses UpdateExpression without a condition. No version field, no optimistic locking, no ETag support.
findings.gap: Concurrent agent instances writing to the same SKU will silently overwrite each other's changes with no conflict detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a version attribute and use DynamoDB conditional writes (ConditionExpression: version = :expected) to detect concurrent modifications.

compensating_controls: Add version attribute with DynamoDB conditional writes
Limit concurrent agent instances to 1 per resource scope during pilot

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No explicit rate limiting is configured in the SAM template. The HTTP API has no ThrottlingBurstLimit or ThrottlingRateLimit properties. No WAF rules are defined. API Gateway HTTP API default account-level throttle (10,000 rps) is too high to protect against agent loops.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop could execute thousands of mutations per second with no service-level protection.
findings.recommendation: Configure explicit throttling on the HTTP API route (ThrottlingBurstLimit, ThrottlingRateLimit) in infra/template.yaml and consider per-client throttling via WAF.

compensating_controls: Add API Gateway route-level throttling (e.g., 100 rps)
Add WAF rate-based rule scoped to /graphql endpoint

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No per-agent transaction limits are configured. While mutations operate on single records (one SKU per call), there is no mechanism to cap total operations per agent identity per time window.
findings.gap: No configurable business transaction limits (e.g., max mutations per hour per caller identity).
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller mutation rate tracking that rejects requests exceeding configurable thresholds.

compensating_controls: Implement per-client mutation counting using DynamoDB atomic counters
Monitor mutation volume via CloudWatch metrics and alert on anomalies

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: All mutations commit immediately. upsertProduct writes directly to DynamoDB with active: true. deleteProduct immediately sets active=false. No draft, pending, or proposed state exists in the data model.
findings.gap: An agent cannot propose a change for human review before it takes effect. All writes are immediately committed.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Product schema with a status field supporting DRAFT/PENDING states, and add a confirmProduct mutation that transitions from PENDING to ACTIVE.

compensating_controls: Add status field to Product schema (DRAFT, PENDING_REVIEW, ACTIVE)
Implement approval queue at orchestration layer

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval workflow exists. Mutations execute immediately without any configurable approval step. No Step Functions with human approval tasks.
findings.gap: High-risk operations cannot be gated behind human approval at the application layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates for mutation types that exceed risk thresholds.

compensating_controls: Implement approval gates at agent orchestration layer
Use Step Functions with waitForTaskToken for high-risk mutations

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Apollo Server returns structured GraphQL errors but the requireScope function throws a generic new Error('forbidden: ...') resulting in extensions.code: INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR for permission errors. No retryable indicator exists in error responses.
findings.gap: Error codes are inconsistent (permission errors appear as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) and have no retryable indicator.
findings.recommendation: Replace throw new Error(...) with throw new GraphQLError('...', { extensions: { code: 'FORBIDDEN' } }) and add a retryable boolean in extensions.

compensating_controls: Agents can pattern-match on error message text
Apollo error middleware could classify errors post-hoc

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: The GraphQL schema (schema/catalog.graphql) is well-documented but has no versioning scheme. No version identifier, no changelog, no breaking change detection tooling, no consumer-driven contract tests.
findings.gap: Schema changes could break agent tool bindings silently with no detection mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Add schema versioning and integrate breaking change detection (e.g., graphql-inspector diff) in CI.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to specific schema snapshots
Add graphql-inspector schema validation to CI

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: X-Ray tracing is active (Tracing: Active in SAM template Globals). However, no structured logging library is configured — no JSON logger, no correlation_id field, no request_id propagation in application logs.
findings.gap: Tracing exists but structured logging with correlation IDs is absent. Cannot correlate application logs with specific agent-initiated requests.
findings.recommendation: Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger with structured JSON output and inject API Gateway request ID as correlation ID.

compensating_controls: Lambda automatically logs request ID to CloudWatch
Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms are defined in the SAM template. No anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, no SLO-based alerting configured.
findings.gap: API degradation or elevated error rates will not be detected automatically.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda errors (>1% error rate), p99 latency (>5s), and throttles.

compensating_controls: Lambda publishes error/duration metrics automatically
Add alarms manually or via separate IaC

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Infrastructure is defined as SAM/CloudFormation (infra/template.yaml). However, no evidence of peer review requirements (no CODEOWNERS file) or drift detection (no AWS Config rules).
findings.gap: IaC exists (sub-check 1 passes) but change review enforcement and drift detection are not evidenced.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS with mandatory review for infra/ and enable CloudFormation drift detection.

compensating_controls: Add CODEOWNERS requiring review for infra/ changes
Enable AWS Config for drift detection

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists in the repository. No .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or any pipeline definition was found.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline to test, validate, or deploy the service. No mechanism to catch API-breaking changes before production.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline + CodeBuild) that runs tsc, vitest, and GraphQL schema validation.

compensating_controls: Manual deployment via SAM CLI
Add minimal CI pipeline with schema validation

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No deployment automation or rollback mechanism is configured. No blue/green, no canary, no Lambda alias traffic shifting, no CodeDeploy configuration.
findings.gap: A broken deployment cannot be automatically rolled back.
findings.recommendation: Add DeploymentPreference with Canary10Percent5Minutes and alarm-triggered rollback to the SAM function.

compensating_controls: SAM supports --no-execute-changeset for manual review
Lambda versioning and alias-based rollback can be added

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: The vitest test framework is configured as a devDependency and a test script exists in package.json. However, no test files (.test.ts, .spec.ts) were found in the repository.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage for the GraphQL API.
findings.recommendation: Create tests covering valid queries, mutation authorization, idempotency behavior, pagination, and error responses.

compensating_controls: Manual testing via GraphQL playground
Add integration tests with Apollo executeOperation

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No separate environment configurations, no docker-compose for local testing, no seed data scripts, no staging-specific SAM configuration.
findings.gap: No sandbox or staging environment for testing agent behavior with production-equivalent data shape.
findings.recommendation: Add samconfig.toml with staging and production environments, and create a seed data script.

compensating_controls: Deploy separate SAM stack with staging prefix
Use DynamoDB local for integration testing

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Products have an updatedAt field set to ISO 8601 UTC timestamp on every write. However, there is no createdAt timestamp, and the products query uses DynamoDB scan which is eventually consistent by default with no freshness signaling to the caller.
findings.gap: No creation timestamp. No data freshness signaling for eventually-consistent scan results.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt timestamp on initial creation and document/signal data consistency level in responses.

compensating_controls: Add ConsistentRead: true to scan operation
Document consistency model in schema

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission mechanism exists. State changes (upsert, delete) are not published to SNS, EventBridge, SQS, or any event bus.
findings.gap: No reactive notification mechanism for catalog changes.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding DynamoDB Streams with a Lambda subscriber that publishes events to EventBridge.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limit documentation exists. The API does not return X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After, or similar headers. No API Gateway usage plan is configured.
findings.gap: Agents cannot discover rate limits programmatically.
findings.recommendation: Document rate limits and add rate limit response headers via API Gateway response parameters.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Not a data-handling target. The system stores product catalog data only: SKU, name, description, priceCents, currency, active status, and updatedAt. No PII/PHI/financial/credential data is stored, processed, or logged.
findings.gap: None — product catalog data does not contain sensitive information.
findings.recommendation: Reassess if user-specific data is added in the future.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Stage A = No: system stores product catalog data only, no sensitive data. Evaluated as INFO.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 Stage A determined this is not a data-handling target. Product catalog fields (SKU, name, price, currency) contain no PII, PHI, financial instruments, or credentials.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality metrics, completeness monitoring, or freshness SLAs are defined for the product catalog data.
findings.gap: No visibility into data completeness or quality issues.
findings.recommendation: Monitor null rates for optional fields and establish freshness expectations.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No formal data catalog exists. The GraphQL schema serves as basic metadata documentation for the product catalog domain.
findings.gap: No centralized data catalog for cross-service discovery.
findings.recommendation: Adequate for single-service scope. Consider formal catalog if domain spans multiple services.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics published. Only default Lambda/API Gateway infrastructure metrics available.
findings.gap: Cannot measure business outcomes of agent interactions with the catalog.
findings.recommendation: Add custom CloudWatch metrics for catalog operations (products_created, products_deleted, query_volume).

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: Documented GraphQL interface via schema/catalog.graphql served through API Gateway HTTP API.

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema file (schema/catalog.graphql) is the machine-readable specification with typed definitions.

evaluations.title: Idempotent Write Operations
evaluations.reason: Both mutations are idempotent: upsertProduct uses PutItem by SKU (overwrite), deleteProduct sets active=false (repeatable).

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: All responses are structured JSON via GraphQL protocol with client-controlled field selection.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered. No operations >30s or long-running workflows in this catalog service.

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: Cognito JWT authorizer configured on API Gateway. JWT claims extracted with scope parsing. Supports machine identity via client_credentials flow.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: OAuth scopes differentiate read (any authenticated) from write (catalog:write). Lambda IAM role scoped to specific DynamoDB table.

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Action-level enforcement via requireScope check: queries open to any authenticated client, mutations require catalog:write scope.

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: No hardcoded credentials. Lambda uses IAM role via default credential chain (automatic rotation). No secrets in environment variables.

evaluations.title: Agent Identity Suspension
evaluations.reason: Cognito supports immediate identity suspension (disable user, global sign-out, revoke tokens). API Gateway validates JWT on every request.

evaluations.title: Compensation and Rollback
evaluations.reason: All mutations are single-step atomic DynamoDB operations. deleteProduct is a soft-delete (inherently reversible). PITR enabled for table-level recovery.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: Current state fully queryable via product(sku) and products(limit, cursor) GraphQL queries.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered. Service's sole dependency is its own DynamoDB table — does not call other microservices or external APIs.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered. No P0 priority designation or critical path identification provided.

evaluations.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
evaluations.reason: Product catalog data (SKU, name, price, currency) is not subject to data residency or sovereignty requirements. No regulated personal data.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Cursor-based pagination with configurable limit (default 50). GraphQL field selection enables targeted queries.

evaluations.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema enforces type validation at API boundary. Required fields (ID!, String!, Int!) validated by Apollo Server. Structured validation error responses.

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: System stores product catalog data only (no PII). No user-identifiable information in the data model or logs.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are human-readable and semantically meaningful: sku, name, description, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB table has SSEEnabled: true. Point-in-Time Recovery also enabled ensuring backup encryption.

items.summary: Resolve the audit logging BLOCKER and address the most critical safety risks: concurrency controls, rate limiting, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Address remaining safety risks (identity propagation, blast radius) and build quality foundations (CI/CD, observability, error handling).
Improve test coverage, add event-driven patterns, and enhance operational metrics.
Informational improvements: data quality monitoring and formal catalog when needed.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy immutable audit logging for mutations
recommended_actions.rationale: Only BLOCKER — must resolve before any agent deployment. Add structured audit log capturing principal, action, resource, timestamp.

recommended_actions.action: Add API Gateway throttling and rate limiting
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents runaway agent loops from overwhelming the service. Quick win — configuration change in SAM template.

recommended_actions.action: Implement optimistic locking on DynamoDB writes
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents silent data corruption from concurrent agent instances writing to same SKU.

recommended_actions.action: Add draft/pending state and approval workflow
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables human oversight for agent-initiated catalog changes. Critical safety control for write-enabled agents.

recommended_actions.action: Create CI/CD pipeline with schema validation
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables automated testing, breaking change detection, and safe rollback — foundational engineering maturity.
Makes agent-initiated requests debuggable and enables proactive detection of service degradation.
